nodes.title: Confirm what the load flagged, and size it
nodes.purpose: Which shipments have lost their outlet, which approvals run out, which streams are under the floor, and by how much.
nodes.how: Every open manifest against the bookings of its unit for the week it arrives; every approval against its expiry; every approved stream against the floor at the fees in force. Limited to what the load that fired the rule changed.
nodes.check: Every flagged position recomputes from the bookings, the approvals and the price book.

nodes.title: Why it happened, and whether anyone is on it
nodes.purpose: Is this new, and is someone already handling it.
nodes.how: The outage notice, the fee change, the approval expiry, and what the plant managers, the service centers and transport have said.
draws: Gmail: outage, outlets, pricing (F1, F2, F3, B1)
nodes.check: Every cause is dated and sourced.

nodes.title: Look across the network: headroom, holds, outlets, clauses
nodes.purpose: What the rest of the network can take, what can wait, and what the contracts allow.
nodes.how: For each shipment: units with the codes on their permit and headroom in the week, the extra cost on the rate card, the ten-day clock at the service center, the approved third-party outlets; for each stream under the floor, the pass-through clause.
nodes.check: No unit is loaded past its headroom; no hold runs past its tenth day.

nodes.title: What can still be done, including nothing
nodes.purpose: Each course of action with what it costs and what it protects, checked against open goals.
nodes.how: Each option with its cost, the shipments it covers, the revenue it protects, who has to agree, and an honest statement where a load can simply wait; read the open goals on this role.
nodes.check: Every option states what it costs and what it covers.

nodes.title: Notice to the people you chose
nodes.purpose: One page, sent without waiting for you.
nodes.how: The shipments, why they lost their outlet, what the network holds, the options and the moves; on the re-route notice template.
nodes.check: Every figure in the notice links back to its step.

recs.title: Re-route nine shipments to Granger and one to Northstar, hold two on the pad, bring the overflow home, bill the fee
recs.summary: Walt Brennan confirms the Granger slots for weeks 45 and 46, Hector Ruiz books the trucks from Thursday, Jenna Fairbanks holds the two loads whose clocks reach 15 November, Carla Dimitriou moves the two Meridian West profiles to Granger, and the account managers bill the Illinois fee on the next Riverbend invoices under clause 9.2.
recs.tradeoff: Granger runs close to its organic-liquids headroom for two weeks, and the two held loads depend on the kiln being back on 15 November as estimated.

story.text: The rule fired: 18 positions need a decision after the Port Terrell kiln went down. What can still be done?
Read every open manifest against the outage weeks and every hold against its clock.
The kiln failed on 3 November; two approvals and two floor positions were already flagged.
Read the policy: a permitted code is not an outlet without capacity; a hold leaves within ten days.
Granger's headroom covers most of it; Northstar the organic liquids beyond it.
The overflow streams cost less at Granger than at Meridian West.
Move what the network can take, hold what can wait, bring the overflow home, and bill the fee.

recs.title: Send everything stranded to third-party outlets
recs.summary: Leave Granger's bookings as they are and send the stranded shipments to Northstar Thermal and Meridian West at their outlet cost.
recs.tradeoff: Keeps Granger's headroom, but the aqueous loads with a destruction requirement have no outlet outside the network, six shipments go negative, and Meridian West's approvals end this month.

story.text: Could the outlets take it all?
No outlet takes the aqueous loads with a certificate of destruction.
Only as a fallback if Granger will not confirm the slots.

recs.title: Ask the generators to hold their shipments until 16 November
recs.summary: Hold every inbound load at the generator or on the pad until the kiln is back; nothing moves.
recs.tradeoff: Costs nothing in haul, but breaches six ten-day clocks at Galena Shores, defers the revenue, and two generators have contractual pickup windows this week.

story.text: The first clock runs out on 11 November.
Only for the loads whose clock reaches the restart.
